channel.title: MIND / MATTER Daily Briefing
channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: A Transdisciplinary Science of Information within the Organogram of Consciousness
item.description: Information transcends the traditional disciplines of physics, psychology, cosmology, and biology, yet remains connected to them through Zero-Point Energy. Although the origins of space, time, and matter are known, the when and how of Information’s emergence remain elusive.

item.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
item.description: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future $e^+e^-$ colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes $e^+ e^- \to t\bar{t},\ e^+e^-\to μ^+μ^-$ and Bhabha scattering $e^+e^-\to e^+e^-$, representing the mass threshold behavior, the $Z$ pole resonance and the $s/t$-channel interplay.

item.title: Nambu’s Dynamics, Strings, and Gravitized Quantum Theory
item.description: In this article, we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory.

item.title: Body in memory: the role of bodily self-consciousness in episodic memory and autonoetic consciousness
item.description: Episodic memory (EM) enables the conscious recollection of personally experienced events, including contextual features such as visual, auditory and emotional details. However, the role of bodily signals has been largely neglected in EM, although the observer's body provides a rich bodily context during the encoding, storage and recall of events, and has recently been associated with a bodily form of self-consciousness (bodily self-consciousness; BSC).

item.title: Mind your head: Entropic Brain, irruption theory and the intelligibility problem
item.description: Abstract The entropic brain hypothesis (EBH) and irruption theory (IT) are two recent frameworks to investigate consciousness by examining neural entropy. While they differ in their theoretical commitments, both aim to advance neuroscientific investigations of consciousness without succumbing to the intelligibility problem: the impossibility for scientific inquiries to provide intelligible access to subjective experience.

item.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
item.description: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron's position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today.

item.title: Optimizing interference zeros for finite-pulse transmission in waveguide quantum electrodynamics
item.description: A photon pulse occupies a range of frequencies, so suppressing reflection at its carrier need not minimize the error of the transmitted pulse. We study two separated emitters coupled to a common waveguide at several contact points.

item.title: Therapeutic communication: avoidance of negative influences and application of beneficial suggestions in anesthesia and intensive care, emergency, and pain medicine
item.description: In anesthesia, and in emergency and intensive care medicine a “therapeutic communication” with the patient is needed that exceeds mere information exchange and that supports patient and treatment. First, ever-present nocebo effects and negative suggestions must be avoided or neutralized.

item.title: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
item.description: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear.

item.title: Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One
item.description: The claim that interactions with artificial conversational agents merely simulate human conversation rests on a philosophical distinction between reproducing the observable features of an activity and actually performing it. Although this distinction is appropriate for certain physical phenomena, its application to linguistic and symbolic activities is far less straightforward.

item.title: Noetics, a New but Old Understanding of Mind and Reality
item.description: Noetics is examined here as an interdisciplinary approach to how lived experience becomes a knowledge claim and informs action. This narrative review brings historical philosophy into dialogue with cognitive science, contemporary theories of consciousness, contemplative traditions, and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Actualization and the Quantum Mechanical Universe: Dissolving the Gap
item.description: The actualization gap—the apparent discontinuity between the classical probability distribution delivered by decoherence and the single definite outcome that appears in experience—has been treated in the foundations literature as an outstanding problem in the physics of quantum measurement. This paper argues that the gap is not a physical problem and admits no physical solution.

item.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
item.description: Abstract This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

item.title: Virtual reality as a neural state-modulating technology: EEG complexity during VR gameplay versus VR gameplay viewing
item.description: Pharmacological agents and brain stimulation can modulate conscious states, but offer limited control over the structure of the experience itself. Virtual reality (VR) can alter subjective experience while allowing its structure to be experimentally controlled.
